Anan Ashraf

TSLA
NVDA

Trading disclosure

EMAG designs and builds precision equipment for turning, grinding, and gear cutting, primarily serving the automotive industry.

The company has also developed specialized systems for manufacturing high-precision gears used in humanoid robot actuators.

Tesla, meanwhile, has begun early production of its Optimus humanoid robots at its production line at its Fremont factory.

Shares of EV giant Tesla (TSLA) rose on Friday, adding to a strong weekly performance, as the company reportedly plans to acquire Germany-based machine-tool maker EMAG.

TSLA stock started the short Thanksgiving week strong, thanks to a tech rally driven by the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO in less than two weeks of his ouster. The stock clocked small losses in the following two days, before jumping on Friday.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

TSLA stock was up more than 5% at market close. It has gained nearly 16% overall this week, with anticipation for a deal between the company and SpaceX adding optimism, clocking its best week since May 2025, according to Koyfin data.

Tesla Eyes German Machine Maker

Tesla submitted plans to Germany's competition authority without providing details of the transaction, Automotive World reported on Friday. The filing follows Tesla's registration of Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE, a shell company renamed from an August entry, with its address at EMAG's headquarters in Salach near Stuttgart, the report noted.

EMAG designs and builds precision equipment for turning, grinding, and gear cutting, primarily serving the automotive industry by producing machines that make drivetrain components such as transmissions and related parts. The company has also developed specialized systems for manufacturing high-precision gears used in humanoid robot actuators.

Deal Talks As Tesla Ramps Up Cybercab, Optimus Production

The news comes as Tesla has started early production of its Optimus humanoid robots at a production line at its Fremont factory, designed for up to one million units a year. On the third-quarter (Q3) earnings call, CEO Elon Musk reiterated that the hand of the robot is the main hardware challenge. The company is aiming to deliver the robots to external customers starting in late 2027.

Tesla's sole European vehicle plant in Grünheide, Brandenburg, currently builds Model Y vehicles at roughly 375,000 annual capacity. The company recently announced a first €3 billion investment in the factory to produce up to one million Cybercab robotaxis a year there as well, with construction targeted for 2027 and production from 2029. Cybercab production is currently limited to the company's factory in Texas.

title: Tesla Rallies 5% Amid SpaceX Merger Speculation; Rivian and SpaceX Rise 3%: Is Tesla’s 439x P/E a Warning Sign?
detail:
Tesla Rallies 5% Amid SpaceX Merger Speculation; Rivian and SpaceX Rise 3%: Is Tesla’s 439x P/E a Warning Sign?
David Moadel
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 9:04 AM PST 6 min read
TSLA
SPCX
RIVN
LCID
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

Tesla jumped 5% on reported SpaceX merger talks, with HSBC estimating a $507 per share offer, though no deal exists and the exchange ratio looms large.

Rivian climbed 3% despite sitting outside the talks and remaining down 39% this year, while Lucid slipped amid its Saudi-backed turnaround.

Tesla's 439x earnings multiple leaves little cushion: operating income fell 56% last quarter as R&D surged, and Gary Black warns an all-stock bid could sink SpaceX below $100.

Read: Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps with, and it is free today. Read more here.

Merger speculation is lifting Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stock after the Thanksgiving break, putting a spotlight on how much the market already pays for the company's earnings. TSLA stock is at $397.87 in midday trading, up 5%. After that gain, the stock is still down 12% year to date (YTD).

Pascal Le Segretain / Getty Images Entertainment via Getty Images

The rocket and satellite company on the other side of the reported deal is climbing too. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) stock is at $131.20, up 3%. Electric vehicle (EV) maker Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ:RIVN) is moving higher as well. Rivian stock is trading at $12.07, up 3%.

No deal has been announced, and retail forums are split between traders hoping for a buyout premium and those fearing dilution or terms that favor SpaceX. Both camps are focused on one number for Tesla: the exchange ratio.

What's Been Reported on Tesla and SpaceX Deal Talks

Tesla and SpaceX have reportedly assembled deal teams. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are advising SpaceX directors Roelof Botha and Randy Glein, while Evercore is advising Tesla Chair Robyn Denholm and directors Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung, the Financial Times reported. The core question is how many SpaceX shares Tesla shareholders would get for each share they own.

Credit: Getty Images

The main equity indexes were all up after a short and relatively quiet post-Thanksgiving trading session. So were all 11 stock market sectors, as consumer discretionary led the way higher on Black Friday.

"With Silicon Valley and the rest of the U.S. on holiday yesterday, markets have been experiencing a quiet 24 hours," observes Deutsche Bank Global Head of Macro Research Jim Reid, though he also sees "some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets."

Reid cites another "wild ride" for South Korea's KOSPI Index, which is heavy with semiconductor stocks and was up 4.3% on Friday, as well as "strong gains" for Japan's Nikkei (+2.1%) and a rally for tech stocks in Europe.

Nvidia (NVDA, +0.8%) bounced late and finished in the middle of the pack among Dow Jones stocks, as receding AI fear ultimately overcame company-specific loathing.

Indeed, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) was up 4.2% today, as other chipmakers caught plenty of bids. And Anthropic (ANT) surged 11% in further affirmation of renewed faith in the broader AI trade.

Track all markets on TradingView

The Cboe Volatility Index ticked up to 27.52 from 26.80 on Thursday (most futures markets trade 24 hours, five days a week) before easing back to 24.44. The fear index remains outside its "normal" range between 12 and 20.

At the same time, the 10-year Treasury yield was up 8.8 basis points to 4.936%, as investors sold "risk off" assets in favor of "risk on" assets. Note that bond yields and bond prices move in opposite directions.

By the closing bell, the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average had added 1.2% to 50,774, the broad-based S&P 500 was up 1.6% at 7,297, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite had risen 2.3% to 24,129.

Will SpaceX and Tesla merge?

You won't find it on the earnings calendar or the economic calendar for next week. But we should talk about the agenda for Tesla's (TSLA, +5.2%) annual meeting on Thursday, December 3, and whether it'll include discussion of a merger with SpaceX (SPCX, +4.8%).

Track all markets on TradingView

The Financial Times reported this week that five directors from two special committees formed by each of the Elon Musk entities on October 20 are discussing an all-stock deal that would value a combined company at about $3.5 billion.

Track all markets on TradingView

On November 18, Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin of The New York Times the two companies "don't need" a merger, but he answered "probably, yes" when Sorkin asked if they'd be better together.

Berenberg slashed AST SpaceMobile's price target 67% to $30 over launch delays, yet the stock still rose 2% while Rocket Lab jumped 5%.

SpaceX's FCC approval for a million-satellite data center plan competes with fears that a Tesla all-stock merger bid could drag shares below $100.

Blue Origin's New Glenn return to flight is the swing factor that could force Berenberg to revisit its Hold rating on AST SpaceMobile.

Read: Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps with, and it is free today. Read more here.

Space stocks are bouncing back ahead of the holiday-shortened session, and one of the more surprising gains belongs to a name Wall Street just turned conservative on. AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) stock is at $26.47 in morning trading, up 2%. That move comes even after a Berenberg downgrade, and it leaves the direct-to-cell satellite company down 64% year to date (YTD).

Marco Bello/Getty Images

Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) stock is at $49.23, up 5%, after a successful Electron launch on Thanksgiving night. Cathie Wood-backed SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) stock is at $131.10, up 3%, following a busy run of headlines. Technology is leading a broad rebound, with NASDAQ 100 futures up sharply.

The bigger question is whether Berenberg's caution on AST SpaceMobile is a warning for the whole group, or a sign that space stocks are shaking off November's selloff. Each of these three companies is moving for its own reason.

Berenberg Slashes AST SpaceMobile Target Over Launch Delays

Berenberg downgraded AST SpaceMobile to Hold from Buy on November 27 and cut its price target to $30 from $92. That 67% reduction from Berenberg reflects satellite launch delays that push back the company's revenue growth. Under its new model, Berenberg expects about 100 satellites deployed by 2028, held at that level until positive free cash flow in 2030. A faster build toward 248 satellites was Berenberg's earlier expectation.
